title: Maybe Find
story: You're searching for a letter inside a string � like finding the '@' in an email address. Sometimes you find it (with its position), sometimes you don't. Instead of returning -1 for "not found" (easy to forget to check), you return a clear enum that forces the caller to handle both cases.
why: An enum for search results eliminates the magic number -1 and makes missing values explicit.
analogy: FindResult is like tracking a package. "Found" means the courier has your package and tells you which shelf it's on (position). "NotFound" means the warehouse is empty. You can't open "NotFound" expecting contents � the courier forces you to look inside first.
try_it: Search for different letters in "chocolate": try 'o', 'x', 'c', 'e'. Add a `find_all` concept that tracks multiple positions. Add a `FoundFirst(position: Int)` variant that only stores position (not the item).
tips: Name the enum after what it represents: `FindResult` tells readers "this is a search outcome"
Use `_` to ignore the found item when you only care about the position
The NotFound variant needs no data � "not found" is a complete answer
common_mistakes: Trying to access `.position` directly on a FindResult without matching first � it might be NotFound
Returning -1 from the search function instead of using an enum � that defeats the purpose of type safety
